scope: First chapter authoring briefs only; no textbook body or execution claim

sections.title: Problems, inputs, and observable outputs
sections.question: What can a computation be asked to return?
sections.entry: Basic Python variables, lists and the distinction between a question and one input instance.
sections.exit: Specify input representation, observable output, success criterion and resource boundary for one task.
sections.worked_case: A bitstring task versus a repeated-sampling expectation-estimation task; state which quantities are outputs and which are model internals.
sections.boundary: No new quantum law is asserted. Distinguish a sample, an estimated statistic and simulator-only state inspection.
sections.code_plan: Complete reference: examples/foundations/task_contracts.py; standard library only, no quantum backend required.
sections.independent_check: A classical enumerated reference and a deliberately mismatched output contract.
sections.transfer_task: Give a new task and ask the reader to identify what must be measured and how success would be checked.
sections.next_transition: Independent mathematical and target-reader review; the author-checked draft may support drafting 1.2 under local start checks.

sections.title: A first interference experiment
sections.question: How can two alternatives cancel?
sections.entry: 1.1 and arithmetic on two real numbers; all preview notation is introduced locally.
sections.exit: Predict recombination and distinguish adding amplitudes from adding probabilities.
sections.worked_case: A fully displayed two-component, two-step interference calculation with every sum written out; a changed relative sign changes the prediction.
sections.boundary: Use an explicitly labelled preview model. The formal state postulate is owned by 3.1 and the measurement postulate by 6.1; do not cite those future sections as missing prerequisites or claim to derive a physical postulate.
sections.code_plan: Complete independent real-matrix reference and released FlagQuantum 0.3.1 comparison: examples/foundations/interference.py.
sections.independent_check: Hand-computed multiplication and cancellation, followed by a deliberate probability-addition error.
sections.transfer_task: Predict a changed sign or missing recombination step and explain which arithmetic step changes.
sections.next_transition: Independent mathematical and target-reader review; the explained, author-checked draft may support drafting 1.3 under local start checks.

sections.title: What a quantum state describes
sections.question: What information does a state description contain?
sections.entry: 1.2, including the locally introduced two-component preview.
sections.exit: Distinguish the mathematical state description, a measurement choice and data collected over repetitions.
sections.worked_case: Two preview descriptions with the same immediate outcome frequencies but different later interference.
sections.boundary: Keep this a conceptual preview; complex-space definitions belong to Chapter 2, formal equivalence to 3.1 and measurement statistics to Chapter 6.
sections.code_plan: Complete program examples/foundations/state_descriptions.py reuses the 1.2 independent matrix reference, verifies released FlagQuantum predictions and labels data as a constructed fixture.
sections.independent_check: Predict-first comparison of immediate measurement and subsequent recombination.
sections.transfer_task: Explain why an output histogram alone need not determine all future predictions.
sections.next_transition: Independent mathematical, implementation and target-reader review remain pending. Next drafting assignment is 1.4, whose exact prerequisite remains 1.1.

sections.title: Algorithms, simulators, and physical devices
sections.question: How do an algorithm, simulator and physical device differ?
sections.entry: 1.1; recall the task/output contract rather than importing hardware engineering.
sections.exit: Identify which object specifies a calculation, emulates it and physically executes a measurement.
sections.worked_case: The same task contract expressed as a program, a tiny numerical calculation and an explicitly proposed physical experiment.
sections.boundary: No hardware execution, provider support or speed ranking is claimed. Statevector inspection is a simulator capability with a separate cost.
sections.code_plan: Plan a complete classical reference and a versioned simulator run when appropriate; hardware access remains optional.
sections.independent_check: A claim checklist that detects substitution of simulator output for measured data.
sections.transfer_task: Classify a changed result or failure as model, numerical, sampling or device evidence.
sections.next_transition: Write a draft only after the local start checks; no body is supplied by this brief.

sections.title: What computational advantage would require
sections.question: What would establish a computational advantage?
sections.exit: Ask for matched problem instances, output accuracy, success probability and full resource accounting.
sections.worked_case: A hypothetical cost comparison that includes preparation, repeated measurements and classical processing, without current performance claims.
sections.boundary: This is an entry-level reasoning contract; formal access/complexity and lower-bound arguments belong to Chapter 14 and later algorithms.
sections.code_plan: A small cost ledger is appropriate; a quantum circuit is not required merely to populate this section.
sections.independent_check: Change one omitted cost or precision requirement and reassess the hypothetical comparison.
sections.transfer_task: Find the missing assumption in a new claimed speedup without requiring an advanced complexity theorem.
sections.next_transition: Write a draft only after the local start checks; no body is supplied by this brief.

sections.title: A map of the learning routes
sections.question: Which learning route serves my question?
sections.exit: Choose a route and identify its entry knowledge and first concrete deliverable.
sections.worked_case: Three bounded destinations: an algorithm prediction, a trainable circuit objective and a program-to-target transformation.
sections.boundary: Present the existing reader routes and core/advanced distinctions, without pretending every volume is a prerequisite for the next.
sections.code_plan: Use linked complete examples only as previews, with their actual draft/validation status.
sections.independent_check: Resolve the selected route against canonical prerequisites and label unstudied advanced branches.
sections.transfer_task: Choose a route for a new task and explain why an unrelated specialization is not required.
sections.next_transition: Write a draft only after the local start checks; no body is supplied by this brief.
